key_insight: A conditional diffusion model can synthesize realistic time-evolving turbulent flame fields from experimental data, preserving major flow and combustion structures across space and time.
engineering_relevance: This offers a data-driven surrogate for exploring flame dynamics, including hard-to-capture regimes like liftoff and reattachment, which can support combustor analysis in data-sparse settings.
method: Uses x-prediction flow matching with a pixel-based spatiotemporal transformer.
Conditions generation on flame regime to produce full spatiotemporal slabs of OH-PLIF and multi-component PIV fields.
Extends to transition synthesis by blending attached and detached denoising velocities over time.
evidence_signal: The generated flames retained key features and statistical consistency, especially at large scales, while errors increased at high temporal frequencies and small spatial scales depending on slab length.
watch_item: Performance appears less reliable for fine-scale, high-frequency details, so careful validation is needed before using outputs for quantitative design decisions.
paper_title: Generating synthetic evolution of turbulent flames with an experimental data-based spatiotemporal diffusion model
